title: Parvati's question: tantra for a hard age
hookLine: the goddess asks how tired, hurried people will find the way
carry: the tantras: a mercy for a hard age
tomorrow: can a busy parent's ordinary day be a spiritual path?
last: BOTH IN THE HAND AT ONCE.

lines: HOW WILL THEY FIND THE WAY?
cards: Some cookbooks give two versions of the big holiday dish: the all-day one, and the weeknight one, for people with jobs and kids and a tired evening. Nobody calls the weeknight version fake.

In the Mahanirvana Tantra, the goddess Parvati worries about something like that. Looking ahead to a hard age, she sees people restless, short on time and strength. The old Vedic rites are long and exacting.
How will they find their way?

teach.b: Shiva doesn't wave the worry away. In the book's telling, he praises her question, because she asks it for everyone's good.

teach.h: A TEACHING FOR THE KALI AGE.
teach.b: The world, he says, moves through ages, down to this one, the Kali age, when life is hardest. For this age, he gives the teaching of the Tantras.
So here, tantra doesn't present itself as a secret for a daring few. It presents itself as a mercy, sized for ordinary, struggling people.
Many Hindus hold a version of that hope: in a hard age, simpler ways are a gift, not a downgrade. Now hold the week up. Dhruva's twelve syllables: the deity in sound.
Lalita's city: the deity in shape.

teach.h: DHRUVA, LALITA, BHRINGI, RAMAKRISHNA, KANNAPPA, JANAKA.
teach.b: Bhringi's bee, and Shiva become half the goddess: never apart. Ramakrishna's cup: the offering, not the substance. Kannappa's eye: a god who truly lives in the temple.
Janaka's palace: enjoyment and freedom in one hand. Each uses the world's own stuff, sound, shape, taste, flame, time, as the way in.
And this book says why it was given at all: because the goddess asked how ordinary people could still get there.

how: The Mahanirvana Tantra is studied by some Hindus in Shakta and tantric lineages, usually with a teacher, and its opening, Shiva answering the goddess, is retold in talks.

games.q: what does “what tantra actually is” mean?
o: a set of long Vedic rites for the most devout
a secret method kept for a daring, chosen few
a teaching given, by its own account, for a hard age

games.q: a goddess's worry, and the answer. tap the pairs.
p: asks how a hurried age will cope
the hard age, in the book
the Tantras, given for this age

s: the Mahanirvana Tantra presents tantra as a secret for a daring few
it presents itself as a mercy for ordinary people in a hard age.

games.q: your grandmother says she's too tired now for the long rites she grew up with, and feels she's failing. in the Mahanirvana's frame, what fits?
o: a path sized for her strength now can still reach the highest.
only the long, exact rites count; she should push through them.
she's done enough; worship isn't meant for this stage of life.
games.why: in the book, Shiva gives the Tantras because the old rites no longer fit people's time and strength: a mercy, not a lesser path.

practice: Close your eyes if that's comfortable, and let one piece of this week come back on its own: a sound, a shape, a taste, a lamp. Rest with whichever arrives first, breathing slowly, and let it be enough.

wordCard.voice: What tantra actually is: here, a teaching the Mahanirvana Tantra says was given for a hurried age, out of care.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the Kali age, the hard age the Mahanirvana Tantra says its teaching is given for.

carryVoice: Carry this: the Tantras, a mercy for a hard age. Parvati asked for all of us, and Shiva said yes. A week, gathered.

sources.ref: Mahanirvana Tantra, chapter 1 (Parvati's question about people of the Kali age; Shiva's praise of the question; the ages of the world; the Tantras' teaching given for the Kali age)
